<!--
  Release notes for SherlockEQ 0.1.3.

  Authored as HTML so Sparkle's update dialog renders the formatting;
  GitHub renders inline HTML in release notes the same way.
-->

<h2>SherlockEQ 0.1.3</h2>

<p>
  A pass over every Equalizer tab — the input (pre-EQ) and post-EQ
  spectra now ride together behind the curve so you can see what
  your correction is actually doing to your music in real time.
  Advanced gets the layer chip strip and tap-to-type gain chips
  that used to be Expert-only, and a dedicated Bypass button
  finally lives on the Equalizer surface itself.
</p>

<h3>Added</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Live input + post-EQ spectrum overlay.</strong>
    The dry input and the post-EQ output spectra are now both
    rendered behind the EQ curve on every Equalizer tab — Simple,
    Speech, Advanced, and Expert. The input layer used to be
    Expert-only (and off by default); it's now on by default
    everywhere. The overlay also takes up more of the canvas
    (50&nbsp;%&nbsp;→&nbsp;70&nbsp;% vertical) so it reads as a real
    background fill rather than a thin ribbon at the bottom.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Bypass button on the Equalizer.</strong>
    A pill toggle now sits at the top of every Equalizer tab — flip
    it to A/B between your tuning and the raw source without leaving
    the screen. Goes red + "Bypassed" when active so you can't lose
    track of which state you're in. Drives the same Reference Mode
    that ⌘B and the popover already used; nothing new to learn.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Layer chip strip on Advanced.</strong>
    Advanced now exposes the same Input&nbsp;/&nbsp;Output&nbsp;/&nbsp;EQ
    curve&nbsp;/&nbsp;Audiogram target&nbsp;/&nbsp;Safety overlay&nbsp;/&nbsp;Peak
    callouts chips that Expert has had. Your chip preferences are
    shared across the two modes — what you toggle in one shows up
    the same way in the other.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Tap-to-type gain chips on Advanced.</strong>
    Each of Advanced's ten octave bands now shows its current gain
    in a small editable chip above the slider. Tap it, type a
    value ("+2.5", "−3", "0", a trailing "dB" is fine), press
    Return — or just click anywhere outside the chip and it
    commits. Esc cancels. Keyboard nudges (±0.5&nbsp;dB) work for
    VoiceOver users too.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Not a medical device</h3>

<p>
  SherlockEQ is not a healthcare or medical application. It does not
  diagnose, treat, measure, or monitor any hearing condition, tinnitus,
  or disability. For concerns about your hearing, consult a doctor,
  audiologist, or licensed healthcare professional.
</p>
